steps.title: Four styles
steps.body: Sercial, grown at higher, cooler sites, gives dry, high-acid wines with citrus and almonds. Verdelho gives medium dry wines, with dried fruit and smoke. Boal gives medium sweet wines, with caramel and raisin. Malvasia, or Malmsey, gives rich, sweet wines, with toffee, coffee and orange peel. All keep high acidity.

steps.title: Age categories
steps.body: Madeira labels show age: 3 years, Finest; 5 years, Reserve; 10 years, Special Reserve; 15 years, Extra Reserve; and 20, 30, 40, 50 years and over. Colheita, or Harvest, comes from a single year, aged at least five years. Frasqueira, or Vintage, comes from a single noble grape and year, aged at least 20 years in cask.

steps.prompt: Match each grape to its style.
steps.explanation: Each noble grape has its style.

steps.title: Old Madeira
steps.body: Some of the oldest wines still drinkable come from Madeira: Frasqueiras from the 19th century appear at auction and are often still vibrant. Producers like Blandy's, Barbeito, Henriques & Henriques and D'Oliveiras keep stocks of old wine. Rainwater, a lighter style, was popular in the US.

steps.prompt: A Frasqueira Madeira must age at least ____ years in cask.
steps.explanation: Twenty years, from a single grape and year.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Sercial, Verdelho, Boal and Malvasia run from dry to rich
Labels show age from 3 years to Frasqueira
Old Madeira can stay vibrant for centuries
